To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The temperature distributions and heat transport in the body injected with nanoparticles are dependent on the volume fraction of nanoparticles and the excitation wavelength and power.
the heat transport through the biological tissue is dependent on many parameters, including thermal conductivity, volume fraction, excitation wavelength, and power.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a numerical tool to study the heat transport through bio-nanofuids and the temperature distributions in the human body subjected to electromagnetic waves, which can be useful in the development and improvement of hyperthermia treatments.
the development of a comprehensive model for the study of heat transport through bio-nanofuids in the presence of electromagnetic fields.

developing an efficient numerical tool for the analysis of the effects induced by electromagnetic waves in biological media and to provide a benchmark for the validation of the numerical models for hyperthermia treatments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the temperature rise in bio-nanofuid (blood with nanoparticle) is higher than that in the bio-fluid alone.

the temperature distribution and heat transport within bio-nanofluid is highly influenced by volume fraction of nanoparticles and metabolic heat generation, and the specific absorption rate of bio-nanoparticle fluid is also influenced by the volume fraction of nanoparticles.

the temperature profiles in the bio-nanofuid are significantly affected by the thermal conductivity, volume fraction and metabolic heat generation of the nanoparticles, and the excitation wavelength and power of the electromagnetic field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the temperature profiles are found to be dependent on the thermal conductivity of biofluid.
, the present study is a first attempt to simulate the temperature profiles in human body subjected to electromagnetic waves and injected with nanoparticles.
, we have developed the model for the heat transport through the bio-nanofuids, which can be applied to the biological systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given electromagnetic wave, the temperature of the human body can be controlled by adjusting the volume fraction of nanoparticles in the blood.
, the temperature distribution in the bio-nanoflowing medium is strongly dependent on the volume fraction of nanoparticles.
the thermal conductivity of blood is a function of volume fraction of nanoparticles and the heat transfer is governed by the thermal conductivity of the blood.
